pairs.locus: Vita Sororis Agnetis, De transitu eius (cap. 11)
pairs.question: Heu me, mater karissima, vt quid filias tuas & me specialiter uis derelinquere! Et quis me miseram consolabitur te, uirgo dulcissima, moriente?
pairs.answer: Ne fleueris, Katherina, quia in breui recipies consolacionem a domino!
pairs.derivation: The dying Agnes is approached by the ailing sister Katherina Erhardi, whose plea contains genuine interrogatives ('vt quid... uis derelinquere', 'quis me miseram consolabitur'). The entire utterance is quoted verbatim and contiguous as the question. Framing dropped before the question: 'uerbaque doloris ingeminans dicebat.' Agnes's reply is quoted in full as the answer; it genuinely answers the 'who will console me' question with 'you will receive consolation from the Lord.' Framing dropped before the answer: 'At uirgo Cristi miseria mota super eam dixit,'. Stopped before the following narration 'Et cum infirma, una cum aliis sororibus instantissime postularet...'. No editorial brackets in either span. Other question-marked exchanges were rejected: the resuscitated soul's 'Cur me reuocas...?' (line 51) receives only an action, not a verbal answer; in the queen's dream-vision (line 113) 'Numquid dormis?'/'non' is trivial and not self-contained, 'Numquid est hic... auia mea sancta Agnes?' is answered only by narration ('sorore hoc affirmante'), and 'Cur pro te orabo?' is answered by a plea/retort rather than a real answer.
